pr_title: fix(nuxt): apply right types to modules and their runtime files
pr_body:

### ❓ Type of change

<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->

- [ ] 📖 Documentation (updates to the documentation, readme or JSdoc annotations)
- [ ] 🐞 Bug fix (a non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] 👌 Enhancement (improving an existing functionality like performance)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (a non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🧹 Chore (updates to the build process or auxiliary tools and libraries)
- [ ] ⚠️ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

### 📚 Description

<!-- Describe your changes in detail -->
<!-- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!-- If it resolves an open issue, please link to the issue here. For example "Resolves #1337" -->

Supports auto import in modules, using the `runtime/` directory as a convention. This helps speed up development and maintains auto import consistent with the rest of nuxt.

Based on the discussion, add the following to `tsconfig.json`:

```json
"inclued": [
  "module/runtime"
],
"exclude": [
  "module/runtime/server"
]
```

add the following to `tsconfig.server.json`:

```json
"inclued": [
  "module/runtime/server"
]
```

issue_context.title: Incorrect types of auto-imports in modules
issue_context.body:
### Environment

------------------------------
- Operating System: Darwin
- Node Version:     v20.5.1
- Nuxt Version:     3.7.0
- CLI Version:      3.7.3
- Nitro Version:    2.6.2
- Package Manager:  pnpm@8.7.1
- Builder:          -
- User Config:      modules, auth, security, typescript, devtools, i18n, postcss, tailwindcss, vue, vite
- Runtime Modules:  nuxt-security@0.14.4, @sidebase/nuxt-auth@0.5.0, @nuxtjs/tailwindcss@6.8.0, nuxt-svgo@3.5.0, @vueuse/nuxt@10.4.1, @nuxtjs/i18n@8.0.0-rc.4
- Build Modules:    -
------------------------------

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/nuxt-starter-xodh6t?file=modules%2Fexample%2Fpages%2Fsomething%2Findex.vue

### Describe the bug

There are missing types from auto-imports, and that the ref, $fetch, or other variables are being inferred as `any` in modules.

### Additional context

_No response_

### Logs

_No response_
comments: _Start a new pull request in [StackBlitz Codeflow](https://stackblitz.com/~/github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/22988?repros=nuxt-starter-xodh6t)._ - [**nuxt-starter-xodh6t** (Open reproduction)](https://stackblitz.com/edit/nuxt-starter-xodh6t?issueRepo=nuxt/nuxt&issueNumber=22988)

This is caused by the fact that we are excluding modules from being covered from the generated tsconfig.

I still think that's a good idea, but it might be worth _either_ adding any added pages/composables/etc. base directories, or possibly automatically including a `./runtime` path within modules (though I realise that's opinionated).

thoughts @pi0 @lihbr @Atinux?

I quite like the `./runtime` convention, despite being opinionated.
This helps extract local modules into dedicated packages that follow conventions(?)
I second @lihbr , I like the `./runtime` convention. And well, Nuxt is convention over configuration :)

Okay, let's do it. We can add `./runtime` path of local module directories to `tsconfig.json`, while adding `./runtime/server` to exclude - and instead add to to the include of `tsconfig.server.json`.

Sorry if I'm asking this in the wrong place. But could this be the reason why the following happens:

If I want to keep developing a module but in an actual running project, I though I could just copy the `src` dir from the dedicated module repo into the `~/modules/myModule` of the running project (while renaming a few things. Like `module.ts` to `index.ts` and `from '@nuxt/kit'` to `from 'nuxt/kit'`.

Or am I totally offtrack?

review_comments: We probably still need to exclude the root module directory, for example if it is a subfolder of the srcDir, e.g. `~/modules/some-module/mod.ts`
